why: The delta a job document's update publishes, and the stored change it is built from. The Go side builds the delivered half from the stored half with the real code, so a change to how a stored path becomes a client path turns it red. The SPA side checks every path the delta names, and every field inside a value set whole, against model-parity/job-schema.json — the list the two sides already agree a job carries — so a name this file invents, a cleared row the model has no place for, or a field the server keeps to itself leaking out, all turn it red without either side copying the other's names. What it cannot catch is a name swapped for a real sibling's, because both resolve; that is a model defect rather than a wire one, and job.parity.test.js and the Go corpus test are where it shows. The entity refs a value carries are restored to the ids a client reads on the way out, which the websocket client shape parity test pins rather than this file.

fields.stored: The change as Mongo reports it, flat: `updatedFields` keyed by dotted stored path, `removedFields` a list of the same. These are the oplog's own words, so the names in them are the ones the document is stored under, not the ones a client reads, and each key is the level Mongo set a value at.
fields.changed: The same change as one entry per path, in the names a client reads, in the order of the stored paths. A client sets each value at its path and replaces what was there — which is why `build.inventionEntries` arriving as `{}` empties the collection rather than merging into it, and why a row set whole drops fields the new row no longer has. A path is dropped entirely when the field it names is one a client is never sent, which is why `protected` is in `stored` and absent here.
fields.removed: The rows that went, each as the path into the job it sat at, in the client's names. The same shape a write sends upward, so one reader of both sees one vocabulary.
fields.revision: The write counter this update itself set — read from `_meta.revision` in `updatedFields`, never from the document looked up after it, which can already be a later write's. An update that sets no revision carries no delta and the whole document travels instead.
fields.appliesTo: The revision this delta applies onto, one below `revision` because a job write increments by exactly one. A client whose held revision is not this one has missed a delivery and reads the job again rather than applying.
